source.title: Mastering Coding: AI and Robotics — Level 4
source.note: Chapter and topic structure follows the updated Teacher Panel curriculum. Topic explanations, learning points and activities are adapted lesson notes, not verbatim textbook transcription. Consult the linked textbook PDF for complete original text, diagrams and exercises.

chapters.title: History of Computers
chapters.description: Explore history of computers through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: People needed tools to make counting and calculations easier.
Early calculating devices used mechanical parts or beads.
An abacus uses beads moved along rods or wires.
Napier’s Bones were used to simplify multiplication and division.

topics.title: Early Calculating Devices
topics.content: The history of computers describes how people developed tools to count and calculate, from simple devices to electronic computers.
learning_points: People needed tools to make counting and calculations easier.
Early calculating devices used mechanical parts or beads.
Modern computers developed through many inventions and improvements.
topics.activity_text: Show students pictures of an abacus, a mechanical calculator and a modern computer.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Abacus and Napier’s Bones
topics.content: The abacus is an early counting device. Napier’s Bones used numbered rods to help perform calculations.
learning_points: An abacus uses beads moved along rods or wires.
Napier’s Bones were used to simplify multiplication and division.
These devices helped people calculate before electronic computers.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate a simple addition using an abacus diagram.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Pascaline and Leibniz Calculator
topics.content: The Pascaline and Leibniz calculator were mechanical calculating machines developed to perform arithmetic operations.
learning_points: Blaise Pascal designed the Pascaline.
The Pascaline performed addition and subtraction.
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed a calculator that could also perform multiplication and division.
topics.activity_text: Compare the operations supported by the Pascaline and Leibniz calculator.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Charles Babbage and Analytical Engine
topics.content: Charles Babbage designed important mechanical computing machines and is often called the Father of the Computer.
learning_points: Babbage designed the Difference Engine.
He also designed the Analytical Engine.
The Analytical Engine included ideas such as input, processing, storage and output.
topics.activity_text: Ask students why Charles Babbage is remembered in computer history.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Herman Hollerith and Early Electromechanical Computers
topics.content: Herman Hollerith developed a punched-card tabulating machine. Later machines such as the Mark I and ENIAC helped move computing towards electronic systems.
learning_points: Punched cards stored information as holes in cards.
Hollerith’s machine helped process census data.
Electromechanical and electronic machines became faster and more capable.
topics.activity_text: Arrange the named machines in a simple historical timeline.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Generations of Computers
topics.content: Computer generations describe major stages in the development of computers, based on changes in their underlying technology.
learning_points: Early generations used large electronic components such as vacuum tubes.
Later generations introduced transistors and integrated circuits.
Modern generations use microprocessors and increasingly powerful technologies.
topics.activity_text: Create a class timeline showing the progression of computer technology.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: GUI Operating System: Windows 10
chapters.description: Explore gui operating system: windows 10 through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Windows 10 is an operating system.
A graphical user interface uses visual elements such as icons, windows and menus.
The interface includes the desktop, Start menu and taskbar.
Windows supports multiple applications and windows.

topics.title: What is an Operating System?
topics.content: An operating system manages computer hardware and software and provides an interface through which users work with a computer.
learning_points: Windows 10 is an operating system.
A graphical user interface uses visual elements such as icons, windows and menus.
The operating system helps users run programs and manage files.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to identify the operating system on a lab computer.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Features of Windows 10
topics.content: Windows 10 provides a graphical environment and tools for working with applications, files and settings.
learning_points: The interface includes the desktop, Start menu and taskbar.
Windows supports multiple applications and windows.
Settings can be changed to suit the user.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate opening an application and switching between windows.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Desktop, Icons and Taskbar
topics.content: The desktop is the main work area. Icons provide shortcuts, while the taskbar gives access to open and pinned applications.
learning_points: The desktop appears after signing in.
Icons represent files, folders, shortcuts or applications.
The taskbar helps users open and switch between programs.
topics.activity_text: Ask learners to identify the desktop, icons and taskbar.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Start Menu and File Explorer
topics.content: The Start menu provides access to applications and options, while File Explorer is used to browse files and folders.
learning_points: Use the Start menu to find and open applications.
File Explorer displays drives, folders and files.
Users can organise and open stored documents.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate locating a document through File Explorer.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Personalising the Desktop
topics.content: Windows allows users to personalise the desktop by changing its background, colours and related appearance settings.
learning_points: Personalisation settings control the desktop appearance.
A picture or colour can be selected for the background.
A screen saver and other appearance options may also be configured.
topics.activity_text: Let students choose an appropriate desktop background in a supervised lab.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Changing Display and System Settings
topics.content: Display and system settings allow users to adjust how Windows looks and behaves.
learning_points: Display settings can change screen resolution and scaling.
System settings provide options for the device and its operation.
Changes should be made carefully and with teacher guidance.
topics.activity_text: Show where display settings are located without changing shared lab settings.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Advanced Features of Word 2016
chapters.description: Explore advanced features of word 2016 through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Text formatting changes the appearance of selected text.
Font effects can emphasise headings and important words.
Line spacing can make text easier to read.
Paragraph spacing separates blocks of text.

topics.title: Text Effects and Formatting
topics.content: Word 2016 includes formatting features that help make documents clear and attractive.
learning_points: Text formatting changes the appearance of selected text.
Font effects can emphasise headings and important words.
Consistent formatting improves readability.
topics.activity_text: Format a short heading and compare it with plain text.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Line and Paragraph Spacing
topics.content: Line spacing controls the vertical space between lines, while paragraph spacing controls space before or after paragraphs.
learning_points: Line spacing can make text easier to read.
Paragraph spacing separates blocks of text.
Spacing options are available from paragraph formatting controls.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate changing line spacing in a short paragraph.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Borders and Shading
topics.content: Borders and shading add visual emphasis to text, paragraphs or parts of a document.
learning_points: A border draws a line around a selected area.
Shading adds a background colour.
Use these features sparingly to keep a document readable.
topics.activity_text: Add a border and light shading to a sample paragraph.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Drop Cap and WordArt
topics.content: Drop Cap enlarges the first letter of a paragraph. WordArt creates decorative text for titles and headings.
learning_points: A drop cap is often used at the beginning of a section.
WordArt provides stylised text effects.
Both features can be adjusted to fit the document.
topics.activity_text: Create a title using WordArt and a paragraph with a drop cap.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Page Layout, Margins and Orientation
topics.content: Page layout settings control the size and arrangement of content on a page.
learning_points: Margins are the blank spaces around the page content.
Orientation can be portrait or landscape.
Columns arrange text in vertical sections.
topics.activity_text: Show the difference between portrait and landscape page orientation.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Columns, Page Numbers and Printing
topics.content: Word 2016 can add page numbers and prepare a document for printing.
learning_points: Page numbers help readers follow longer documents.
Print settings allow users to check page range and copies.
Preview the document before printing.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate inserting page numbers and opening Print Preview.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Introduction to PowerPoint 2016
topics.content: PowerPoint 2016 is presentation software used to communicate information through slides containing text and visual elements.
learning_points: A presentation is made up of slides.
Slides can contain text, pictures and other objects.
Presentations are useful for teaching and explaining ideas.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name situations where a slide presentation is useful.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Starting PowerPoint and Its Window
topics.content: The PowerPoint window provides tools for creating, editing and presenting slides.
learning_points: The Ribbon contains tabs and commands.
The slide pane displays the current slide.
The thumbnail pane helps navigate between slides.
topics.activity_text: Identify the main parts of the PowerPoint window.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Creating a Presentation
topics.content: A new presentation can be created by choosing a design and adding slides for the information to be presented.
learning_points: Start a new presentation.
Choose a suitable theme or blank presentation.
Add slides using appropriate layouts.
topics.activity_text: Create a short three-slide presentation outline.

topics.title: Adding and Formatting Text
topics.content: Text can be added to title and content placeholders or text boxes, then formatted for readability.
learning_points: Use placeholders to enter slide titles and content.
Choose readable fonts and sizes.
Keep slide text concise and organised.
topics.activity_text: Create a title slide and one content slide.

topics.title: Inserting Pictures and Objects
topics.content: Pictures and other objects can make a presentation more engaging and help explain an idea.
learning_points: Insert pictures from an available file.
Resize and position objects carefully.
Use visuals that support the slide topic.
topics.activity_text: Insert one relevant picture into a practice slide.

topics.title: Saving and Running a Slide Show

Open a saved presentation for editing.
Use Slide Show view to present slides to an audience.
topics.activity_text: Save and run the class practice presentation.

learning_objectives: A theme applies coordinated colours, fonts and effects.
A slide layout controls the placement of placeholders.
Background formatting changes the slide background.

topics.title: Applying Themes and Slide Layouts
topics.content: Themes and layouts provide a consistent design and arrangement for slides.
learning_points: A theme applies coordinated colours, fonts and effects.
A slide layout controls the placement of placeholders.
Choose a layout that suits the content.

topics.title: Changing Background and Design
topics.content: The slide background and design can be changed to improve the appearance of a presentation.
learning_points: Background formatting changes the slide background.
Use colours and pictures that keep text readable.
Maintain a consistent style across slides.
topics.activity_text: Choose a simple background for a classroom presentation.

topics.title: Inserting Pictures from a File
topics.content: Pictures from files can be inserted into slides and positioned to support the presentation message.
learning_points: Choose an appropriate image file.
Insert and resize the picture.
Avoid stretching images or covering important text.

topics.title: Adding WordArt and Shapes
topics.content: WordArt and shapes can be used to create decorative headings and simple visual elements.
learning_points: WordArt applies a decorative text style.
Shapes can represent or highlight ideas.
Use decorative elements without overcrowding the slide.
topics.activity_text: Create a heading with WordArt and add one labelled shape.

topics.title: Slide Transitions
topics.content: Slide transitions are visual effects that occur when moving from one slide to another.
learning_points: A transition is applied between slides.
Transition options control the effect and timing.
Use transitions consistently and appropriately.
topics.activity_text: Apply a simple transition to a short slide deck.

topics.title: Applying Animation Effects

topics.content: The Internet is a worldwide network that connects computers and devices so they can share information and services.
learning_points: The Internet connects networks around the world.
It supports communication and information sharing.
People use it for learning, research and many online services.

Websites are accessed using a web browser.

learning_points: Browsers display web pages.
A URL or web address tells the browser where to go.
Different browsers provide similar basic browsing functions.

Check whether information comes from a reliable source.

topics.title: Introduction to Scratch
topics.content: Scratch is a visual programming environment in which users create programs by joining blocks.
learning_points: Scratch uses block-based coding.
Programs are built by connecting instruction blocks.
Projects can include characters, movement and sound.
topics.activity_text: Show a simple Scratch project and identify its blocks.

topics.title: Scratch Window: Stage and Sprites
topics.content: The Scratch window includes the Stage, sprites and areas for creating scripts.
learning_points: The Stage displays the project.
Sprites are characters or objects in a project.
The scripts area is where blocks are joined.
topics.activity_text: Identify the Stage, a sprite and the scripts area.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Programming Palette and Scripts
topics.content: The programming palette contains blocks, and scripts are created by joining suitable blocks in sequence.
learning_points: Blocks are grouped by purpose or category.
A script is a sequence of instructions.
The order of blocks affects what the project does.
topics.activity_text: Join a few blocks to create a simple ordered script.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

Looks blocks change how sprites appear.
Sound blocks play or control sounds.

Control blocks repeat or organise instructions.
Sensing blocks detect conditions or interactions.

topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
topics.content: Artificial intelligence enables computers and devices to perform tasks that usually require human-like abilities such as recognising patterns or responding to information.
learning_points: AI systems use data and programmed methods to perform tasks.
AI is used in many everyday devices.
AI tools can assist people but still need responsible use.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to identify devices they think use AI.

topics.content: A sensor detects information from the surroundings, such as light, movement, temperature or distance.
learning_points: Sensors collect information from the environment.
Devices use sensor readings to respond to conditions.
Different sensors detect different kinds of information.
topics.activity_text: Identify sensors in familiar devices such as phones or automatic lights.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 4 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.
